forms/slider.notes:
`<Slider bind:value={$v} showValue={false} />` leaves only the track; `format` changes the text of the value.

```tsx
<Slider bind:value={$level} track />                                        // a ramp in the control's color
<Slider bind:value={$hue} max={360} track="my-hue-strip" showValue={false}  // .my-hue-strip { background: linear-gradient(…) }
  valueText={(v) => `${v} degrees`} onCommit={remember} aria-label="Hue" />
```

With `track` the input stays a native range (keyboard, forms, screen readers); only its track is cleared and the thumb
drawn. `--m-slider-thumb` on the control (or an ancestor) fills the thumb, e.g. with the picked colour.

A clickable swatch is a `<button>`: give it a `label` (the colour's name), since colour alone says nothing to a screen

The selected ring uses the text colour, so it is visible around any colour; hover motion stops under reduced motion.

forms/time-input.a11y:
A native `<input type="time">`: each part is spin-button editable with the arrow keys and announced by screen readers.

The clock dial opens in a dialog named by `labels.choose` (Alt+ArrowDown in the field opens it too). Its face is a
slider: "Hours", then "Minutes", with the time as its value text; the arrow keys step, Page Up / Down jump (3 hours,
5 minutes), Home / End go to the ends, Enter moves on to the minutes and then closes; Escape closes and returns to the
field. The hour and minute parts on top are toggle buttons that switch the face. Times outside `min` / `max` are
dimmed and cannot be picked.

forms/toggle.a11y:
A `<button role="switch">` with `aria-checked`: Space and Enter toggle it, screen readers announce "on" / "off"; the
label wraps it, so clicking the text toggles too. With `tristate` it is a `role="checkbox"` (a switch has no third
state): `aria-checked="mixed"` while not set.
